title: Aim and objectives

blocks.heading: Aim and objectives
blocks.text: An aim states what the enquiry intends to find out; objectives are specific tasks that help achieve it. Start with a question, then choose measurable objectives and collection steps. A recommendation is a later response, not an observation already established before collection.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Research aim
blocks.text: A research aim is a broad statement of what an enquiry intends to find out, linked to its research question or hypothesis. For a water-access enquiry, the aim might be to investigate return-journey times during the stated week.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Research objective
blocks.text: A research objective is a specific task or target that helps the enquiry achieve its aim. For that aim, record return minutes including waiting for selected households and compare the resulting categories.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Describe how to turn a fictional water-access question into an aim and measurable objectives. Specify return journeys in the settlement during the week; set an aim to investigate time differences, then objectives to record minutes including waiting, group results consistently and compare categories.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect the enquiry to its actual development topic and to Population (7.1) for denominators. Keep an individual record of the real procedure, changes, findings and limits. Fictional models teach the method and must not be presented as the learner’s completed fieldwork.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
